newsitem.title: FRANCE: Offers due for Suez property - paper.
newsitem.headline: Offers due for Suez property - paper.

text.p: French holding group Cie de Suez is about to receive offers for a huge property portfolio but bids from suitors are likely to be far below the net portfolio value of 11 billion francs, L'Agefi newspaper said on Thursday.
L'Agefi said that three groups were in the running, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley in alliance with GE Capital and Unibail and, third, Lehman Brothers, Cargill and UIC.

The financial daily said that, according to its information, the offers were due at Suez on Monday and would range from five and eight billion francs, or between three and six billion short of the net value of the portfolio.
The company was not immediately available for comment.

Suez posted a net attributable loss of 3.96 billion francs in 1995 after a loss of 4.78 billion the year before, mainly because of huge provisions for exposure to property after the bottom fell out of the market in the early 1990s.
It has since sold off Banque Indosuez and put its property assets into a unit, Credisuez, for sell-off.
Chairman Gerard Mestrallet is reorganising the group and has said he expects a return to profit in 1996. He said on September 5 that the group had returned to profit in the first half.
